speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 18)
question: What sounds seat the undivided mind?
premises: String-etc sounding instruments, in longs of ordered abiding.
With undivided mind at each end: supreme-sky-body may be.
inference: In the long tone of ordered sound, undivided mind seats the supreme-sky-body.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 19)
question: How does body-mantra end?
premises: Body-mantra of all, by gross-letter course; half-moon-drop-sound-ending.
From void uttering: may become Śiva.
inference: Void-uttering at the half-moon-drop-sound's end makes Śiva.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 20)
question: Where is sky contemplated?
premises: In own body all directions at once: sky.
Undirected mind: of him, sky all proceeds.
inference: Undirected mind in own body makes sky proceed all through.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 21)
question: Which voids are contemplated?
premises: Back-void, root-void at once, and who?
By body-disregarding power: void-minded may be.
inference: Contemplating back- and root-voids through body-disregard, one becomes void-minded.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 22)
question: What rises from thoughtlessness?
premises: Back-void, root-void, heart-void contemplated steady.
At once from thoughtlessness: thoughtless-rising then.
inference: Steady contemplation of the three voids yields thoughtless-rising.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 23)
question: How long is voidness envisioned?
premises: On body-place, voidness indeed, mere moment should envision.
Thoughtless, thoughtless: sharing thoughtless nature.
inference: A single moment's envisioning makes one share thoughtless nature.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 24)
question: What settles when all is sky?
premises: All gone in body stuff, sky-pervaded, O deer-eyed lady.
Should envision then: of him contemplation, she steady may be.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 25)
question: What is seen inside the body?
premises: Inside body skin-division: become wall, think through.
Not anything inside: meditating, unmeditated-sharer may be.
inference: Seeing the skin as wall with nothing inside makes one the unmeditated-sharer.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 26)
question: Where does the mind enter?
premises: In heart-sky, hidden-eyed, gone mid lotus-casket.
Undivided-minded, O lucky lady: supreme fortune may win.
inference: Mid lotus-casket with undivided mind, supreme fortune is won.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 27)
question: What becomes firm?
premises: From all of own body, at twelve-end, from mind-dissolving.
Of firm-minded made firm: reality-mark proceeds.
inference: Mind-dissolving at the twelve-end sets the reality-mark firm.
